moat_against: Customer concentration at the top of the GLP-1 market (Lilly, Novo set the volumes)
Modality risk — oral GLP-1 formulations would bypass injectable components entirely
Real scaled rivals (Datwyler, Gerresheimer, Stevanato, Aptar) expanding into the same GLP-1 demand
Demand is cyclical at the margin — 2023–24 destocking flattened revenue (3-yr revenue CAGR 2.1%) despite the moat
moat_for: Regulatory lock-in — components spec'd into FDA filings; requalifying a supplier risks the drug's approval and supply
Near-dominant position in elastomer components for GLP-1 injectable pens (Lilly / Novo supply relationships)
Materials-science and quality intangibles (FluroTec via Daikyo) plus efficient scale in a safety-critical niche
Through-cycle economics — OE positive 5/5 years, net cash, mix shifting to High-Value Products (~49% of Q2 revenue)
moat_justification: Components spec'd into FDA drug filings create regulatory lock-in that is expensive and risky to change mid-product-life; scale and materials-science know-how (Daikyo FluroTec) are hard to replicate; dominant elastomer supplier into GLP-1 pens. Held below 8 because the moat protects share, not volume — Lilly/Novo concentration and oral GLP-1 modality risk sit outside it, and credible scaled rivals (Datwyler, Gerresheimer, Stevanato, Aptar) exist.
name: West Pharmaceutical Services, Inc.
one_liner: Excellent business, impossible price — strong 7/10 regulatory-lock-in moat and net cash, but at $374.65 the weighted IRR is 5.0% (IV@15% $65.92); it would need to fall to ~$66 to clear the 15% hurdle.
